In Douala (Week 2, Page 10), Ngo Mbog learns prefixes, suffixes, and describes the weather!

lecons.titre: Consolidating Vocabulary Skills: Synonyms, Antonyms, Prefixes and Suffixes
savoirs_faire: Review and apply synonyms and antonyms in context
Review and apply prefixes and suffixes to build new words
Prepare vocabulary skills for the Term 1 Terminal Assessment

exercices.enonce: Bikoy's teacher in Douala reviews the month's vocabulary skills: synonyms, antonyms, prefixes, and suffixes, using words from occupations like 'teacher' and 'farmer'. Bikoy practices building new words and finding synonyms/antonyms in preparation for the term's final exam.
exercices.astuce: Reviewing synonyms, antonyms, prefixes and suffixes together strengthens vocabulary before an exam.

quiz.question: Which skill combines both synonyms and antonyms understanding?
options: Knowing words that mean the same and words that mean the opposite
quiz.explication: Reviewing synonyms and antonyms together strengthens overall vocabulary understanding.

quiz.question: Why review prefixes and suffixes together?
options: They both help build new words from a base word
quiz.explication: Prefixes and suffixes both change a base word to form new words.

quiz.question: What is this consolidation week preparing pupils for?
quiz.explication: This week reviews vocabulary skills to prepare for the Term 1 Terminal Assessment.

lecons.contenu:
Consolidating Vocabulary Skills: Synonyms, Antonyms, Prefixes and Suffixes

What you will learn:

  • Review synonyms and antonyms
  • Review prefixes and suffixes
  • Prepare for the Term 1 Terminal Assessment

In Douala (Page 10), Bikoy reviews the month's vocabulary skills to prepare for the Term 1 exam!

lecons.titre: Term 1 English Terminal Assessment and Remediation
savoirs_faire: Apply the term's grammar, vocabulary, reading and writing skills
Complete the Term 1 English Terminal Assessment
Review and correct mistakes through remediation

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala administers the Term 1 Terminal Assessment, covering grammar, vocabulary, reading and writing from the whole term. Ekwalla completes the exam and reviews any mistakes with the teacher during remediation.
exercices.astuce: The Terminal Assessment covers all the term's lessons: grammar, vocabulary, reading, and writing.

quiz.question: What does the Term 1 Terminal Assessment cover?
options: The whole term's grammar, vocabulary, reading and writing
A subject not studied this term
quiz.explication: The Terminal Assessment covers the whole term's lessons across all English components.

quiz.question: What happens after the assessment during remediation?
quiz.explication: Remediation reviews and corrects mistakes made during the assessment.

quiz.question: Why is a terminal assessment important?
options: It checks understanding of the whole term's lessons
quiz.explication: A terminal assessment checks understanding of everything learned during the term.

lecons.contenu:
Term 1 English Terminal Assessment and Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Apply the term's English skills
  • Complete the Term 1 Terminal Assessment
  • Review mistakes through remediation

In Douala (Page 11), Ekwalla completes the Term 1 English Terminal Assessment and reviews mistakes!

lecons.titre: Introduction to Decimals, Venn Diagrams, Gain Percentage, and Area of a Parallelogram
savoirs_faire: Read and write decimal numbers
Arrange belongings in a Venn diagram in an orderly manner
Find gain percentage in buying and selling, and calculate the area of a parallelogram

exercices.enonce: Bikoy's teacher in Douala writes '4.5' and explains it as 'four point five'. Bikoy organizes items in a Venn diagram, calculates a gain of 20% on a 1,000 FCFA item = 200 FCFA gain, and finds the area of a parallelogram: base=8 cm, height=5 cm, Area = 40 cm².
exercices.astuce: Area of a parallelogram = base × height. Gain percentage = (gain ÷ cost price) × 100.

quiz.question: How is '4.5' read in words?
quiz.explication: '4.5' is read as 'four point five'.

quiz.question: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 8 cm and height 5 cm?
quiz.explication: Area = base × height = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

quiz.question: What is 20% gain on a 1,000 FCFA item?

lecons.contenu:
Introduction to Decimals, Venn Diagrams, Gain Percentage, and Area of a Parallelogram

What you will learn:

  • Read and write decimal numbers
  • Arrange belongings in a Venn diagram in an orderly manner
  • Find gain percentage in buying and selling, and calculate the area of a parallelogram

In Douala (Week 1, Page 25), Bikoy reads decimals, arranges a Venn diagram, calculates gain percentage, and finds a parallelogram's area!

lecons.titre: Addition and Subtraction of Decimals, Venn Diagram Word Problems, Loss Percentage, and Line Graphs
savoirs_faire: Add and subtract decimal numbers
Represent worded problems in a Venn diagram, and find loss percentage in buying and selling
Use mathematical instruments to draw geometrical shapes, and represent information on a line graph

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala adds '3.25 + 1.50 = 4.75'. Ekwalla solves a Venn diagram word problem, calculates a 10% loss on a 2,000 FCFA item = 200 FCFA loss, and draws a line graph of the week's rainfall.
exercices.astuce: Loss percentage = (loss ÷ cost price) × 100. To add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points.

quiz.question: What is a 10% loss on a 2,000 FCFA item?
What does a line graph show best?
quiz.explication: A line graph is useful for showing how data changes over time.

lecons.contenu:
Addition and Subtraction of Decimals, Venn Diagram Word Problems, Loss Percentage, and Line Graphs

What you will learn:

  • Add and subtract decimal numbers
  • Represent worded problems in a Venn diagram, and find loss percentage in buying and selling
  • Use mathematical instruments to draw geometrical shapes, and represent information on a line graph

In Douala (Week 2, Page 25), Ekwalla adds and subtracts decimals, solves Venn diagram problems, calculates loss percentage, and draws a line graph!

lecons.titre: Multiplication of Decimals, Intersection of Sets, Distance, and Area of a Trapezium
savoirs_faire: Multiply decimal numbers by whole numbers
Solve problems involving the intersection of sets, and calculate distance
Find the area of a trapezium, and present information on a bar chart

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog's teacher in Douala multiplies '2.5 × 4 = 10.0'. Ngo Mbog finds set intersections, calculates a distance of '15 km', and finds the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm, height 4 cm: Area = ½×(6+10)×4 = 32 cm².
exercices.astuce: Area of a trapezium = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height. To multiply a decimal by a whole number, multiply as usual then place the decimal point.

quiz.question: What is 2.5 × 4 ?
What is the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm, and height 4 cm?
What tool best presents a comparison of categories?
quiz.explication: A bar chart is ideal for comparing categories of data.

lecons.contenu:
Multiplication of Decimals, Intersection of Sets, Distance, and Area of a Trapezium

What you will learn:

  • Multiply decimal numbers by whole numbers
  • Solve problems involving the intersection of sets, and calculate distance
  • Find the area of a trapezium, and present information on a bar chart

In Douala (Week 3, Page 26), Ngo Mbog multiplies decimals, finds set intersections, calculates distance, and finds a trapezium's area!

lecons.titre: Division of Decimals, Introduction to Fractions, Speed, and Histograms
savoirs_faire: Divide decimal numbers by whole numbers
Draw, shade, and identify different types of fractions
Calculate speed, and draw and interpret a histogram

exercices.enonce: Bikoy's teacher in Douala divides '9.6 ÷ 3 = 3.2'. Bikoy draws and shades the fraction '3/4', identifies it as a proper fraction, and calculates speed: distance=60 km, time=2 h, Speed = 30 km/h.
exercices.astuce: Speed = distance ÷ time. A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator.

quiz.question: What is 9.6 ÷ 3 ?
If distance is 60 km and time is 2 hours, what is the speed?
quiz.explication: Speed = distance ÷ time = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 km/h.

quiz.question: What is a proper fraction?
options: A fraction where the numerator is smaller than the denominator
quiz.explication: In a proper fraction, the numerator is smaller than the denominator, e.g. 3/4.

lecons.contenu:
Division of Decimals, Introduction to Fractions, Speed, and Histograms

What you will learn:

  • Divide decimal numbers by whole numbers
  • Draw, shade, and identify different types of fractions
  • Calculate speed, and draw and interpret a histogram

In Douala (Week 4, Page 26), Bikoy divides decimals, works with fractions, calculates speed (30 km/h), and reads a histogram!

lecons.titre: Contagious Transmissible Diseases, Types of Fishes, and Sources of Energy
savoirs_faire: State and describe contagious diseases, their mode of transmission and how to prevent/care for them
Name types of fishes and describe their habitats and care
Identify the different sources of energy (sun, water, fuel, wind)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains that contagious diseases like cough spread from person to person, and covering the mouth helps prevent them. Ekwalla then names fish like tilapia and catfish, and identifies the sun and water as sources of energy.
exercices.astuce: Contagious diseases spread from person to person, so covering the mouth when coughing helps prevent spread.

quiz.question: How do contagious diseases spread?
quiz.explication: Contagious diseases spread from person to person, often through coughing or contact.

quiz.question: Which of these is a type of fish?
quiz.explication: Tilapia is a common type of fish.

quiz.question: Which of these is a source of energy?
quiz.explication: The sun is an important source of energy.

lecons.contenu:
Contagious Transmissible Diseases, Types of Fishes, and Sources of Energy

What you will learn:

  • Learn about contagious diseases
  • Name types of fishes
  • Identify sources of energy

In Douala (Week 1, Page 33), Ekwalla learns about contagious diseases, names fish, and identifies energy sources!

lecons.titre: Non-Contagious Transmissible Diseases, Fishing Activities and Methods, and Forms of Energy
savoirs_faire: State and describe non-contagious transmissible diseases, their mode of transmission, prevention and care
Define and describe fishing activities and methods, and state their importance
Identify the different forms of energy (light, heat, sound, electrical)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains that non-contagious transmissible diseases, like malaria, spread through mosquito bites rather than person-to-person contact. Ekwalla then learns about net fishing on the Wouri river, and identifies light and heat as forms of energy.
exercices.astuce: Non-contagious transmissible diseases, like malaria, spread through a carrier (like a mosquito), not direct person-to-person contact.

quiz.question: How does malaria spread?
quiz.explication: Malaria is a non-contagious transmissible disease spread through mosquito bites.

quiz.question: Which of these is a fishing method?
quiz.explication: Net fishing is a common method of catching fish.

quiz.question: Which of these is a form of energy?
quiz.explication: Light is a form of energy.

lecons.contenu:
Non-Contagious Transmissible Diseases, Fishing Activities and Methods, and Forms of Energy

What you will learn:

  • Learn about non-contagious transmissible diseases
  • Learn about fishing activities and methods
  • Identify forms of energy

In Douala (Week 2, Page 34), Ekwalla learns about malaria, discovers fishing methods, and identifies forms of energy!

lecons.titre: Non-Transmissible Diseases: High Blood Pressure, the Fisherman and His Tools, and the Uses of Energy
savoirs_faire: State and describe non-transmissible diseases such as high blood pressure, and how to prevent/care for them
Describe a fisherman and state the tools of a fisherman (net, hook, canoe)
State and discuss the uses of energy (lighting, cooking, transport)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains that high blood pressure is not caught from others but develops from lifestyle, and can be managed by eating less salt. Ekwalla then names a fisherman's tools (net, hook, canoe), and lists uses of energy like lighting a home.
exercices.astuce: High blood pressure is a non-transmissible disease, meaning it cannot be caught from another person.

quiz.question: Is high blood pressure contagious?
quiz.explication: High blood pressure is a non-transmissible disease and cannot be caught from another person.

quiz.question: Which of these is a fisherman's tool?
quiz.explication: A net is a common tool used by fishermen.

quiz.question: Which of these is a use of energy?
quiz.explication: Energy is used for lighting homes, cooking, and transport.

lecons.contenu:
Non-Transmissible Diseases: High Blood Pressure, the Fisherman and His Tools, and the Uses of Energy

What you will learn:

  • Learn about high blood pressure
  • Learn about the fisherman and his tools
  • Discuss the uses of energy

In Douala (Week 3, Page 34), Ekwalla learns about high blood pressure, meets a fisherman, and discusses uses of energy!

lecons.titre: Non-Transmissible Diseases: Diabetes and Obesity, Fish Nutrition and Reproduction, and the Dangers of Energy
savoirs_faire: State and describe diabetes and obesity, their prevention and care
State and explain fish nutrition and reproduction
State and discuss the dangers of energy and how to stay safe

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains that diabetes and obesity are non-transmissible diseases linked to diet and exercise. Ekwalla then learns that fish eat small water plants and insects, and lay eggs to reproduce, and reviews dangers of energy like electric shocks before this month's revision.
exercices.astuce: Diabetes and obesity are linked to diet and exercise habits, not spread from person to person.

quiz.question: What are diabetes and obesity linked to?
quiz.explication: Diabetes and obesity are non-transmissible diseases linked mainly to diet and exercise.

quiz.question: How do many fish reproduce?
quiz.explication: Most fish reproduce by laying eggs.

quiz.question: What is a danger of energy?
quiz.explication: Electric shock is a danger associated with improper use of electrical energy.

lecons.contenu:
Non-Transmissible Diseases: Diabetes and Obesity, Fish Nutrition and Reproduction, and the Dangers of Energy

What you will learn:

  • Learn about diabetes and obesity
  • Learn about fish nutrition and reproduction
  • Discuss the dangers of energy

In Douala (Week 4, Page 34), Ekwalla learns about diabetes and obesity, discovers fish nutrition, and reviews energy dangers!

lecons.titre: Lecture de textes illustrés et les articles partitifs (du, de la, de l', des)
savoirs_faire: Décoder les éléments para-textuels d'un texte illustré
Identifier et utiliser correctement les articles partitifs : du, de la, de l', des
Distinguer l'article partitif de l'article défini dans une phrase

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla à Douala regarde un texte illustré sur les métiers et décode le titre, l'image et la légende. Puis il complète : 'Le boulanger vend DU pain, DE LA farine et DES gâteaux.'
exercices.astuce: L'article partitif indique une quantité indéterminée : du (masculin), de la (féminin), de l' (devant voyelle), des (pluriel).

quiz.question: Quel article partitif convient dans 'Le vendeur a ___ riz' ?
quiz.explication: 'du' est l'article partitif masculin singulier.

quiz.question: Quel article partitif convient dans 'Elle boit ___ eau' ?
quiz.explication: Devant une voyelle, l'article partitif devient 'de l''.

quiz.question: Que permet de décoder un élément para-textuel (titre, image, légende) avant de lire un texte ?
quiz.explication: Les éléments para-textuels aident à anticiper le contenu avant la lecture complète.

lecons.contenu:
Lecture de textes illustrés et les articles partitifs (du, de la, de l', des)

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Décoder les éléments para-textuels d'un texte illustré
  • Identifier et utiliser correctement les articles partitifs : du, de la, de l', des
  • Distinguer l'article partitif de l'article défini dans une phrase

À Douala (Semaine 1, Page 47), Ekwalla décode un texte illustré sur les métiers et apprend les articles partitifs (du pain, de la farine, des gâteaux) !

lecons.titre: Lire des paragraphes de façon expressive et les adjectifs de nationalité
savoirs_faire: Lire des paragraphes de façon expressive en respectant la ponctuation et les majuscules
Identifier et accorder correctement les adjectifs de nationalité
Reconnaître la structure d'un paragraphe (indentation, majuscule initiale, ponctuation finale)

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog à Douala lit à voix haute : 'Mon oncle est camerounais. Sa femme est ivoirienne.' Elle marque une pause à la virgule et baisse la voix au point.
exercices.astuce: L'adjectif de nationalité s'accorde en genre et en nombre : camerounais / camerounaise, ivoirien / ivoirienne.

quiz.question: Comment écrit-on l'adjectif de nationalité au féminin dans 'Elle est camerounais_' ?
quiz.explication: Au féminin, 'camerounais' devient 'camerounaise'.

quiz.question: Que doit-on respecter en lisant un texte de façon expressive ?
quiz.explication: La lecture expressive respecte la ponctuation (pauses) et les majuscules.

quiz.question: Un paragraphe commence toujours par...
quiz.explication: Un paragraphe commence par une majuscule, souvent avec un alinéa.

lecons.contenu:
Lire des paragraphes de façon expressive et les adjectifs de nationalité

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Lire des paragraphes de façon expressive en respectant la ponctuation et les majuscules
  • Identifier et accorder correctement les adjectifs de nationalité
  • Reconnaître la structure d'un paragraphe (indentation, majuscule initiale, ponctuation finale)

À Douala (Semaine 2, Page 48), Ngo Mbog lit des paragraphes à voix haute et apprend les adjectifs de nationalité (camerounais/camerounaise) !

lecons.titre: Textes informatifs, explicatifs et descriptifs : brouillon et révision de l'unité Occupation
savoirs_faire: Utiliser une grille d'évaluation pour améliorer la production d'un texte informatif (1er jet, 2e jet)
Réviser les articles partitifs (du, de la, de l', des)
Réviser les adjectifs de nationalité avant l'évaluation de l'unité

exercices.enonce: Bikoy à Douala écrit un premier jet sur le métier de son père, puis corrige avec la grille d'évaluation pour produire un deuxième jet plus précis, en utilisant 'du travail' et 'un ouvrier camerounais'.
exercices.astuce: Le 1er jet est le brouillon ; le 2e jet est la version corrigée après évaluation à partir de critères précis.

quiz.question: Que fait-on entre le 1er jet et le 2e jet d'un texte ?
options: On corrige à partir d'une grille d'évaluation
quiz.explication: Entre le 1er et le 2e jet, on corrige le texte à partir de critères précis.

quiz.question: Quel type de texte décrit un métier avec des faits précis ?
quiz.explication: Un texte informatif présente des faits et des informations précises.

quiz.question: Quelle est l'orthographe correcte de l'article partitif devant 'travail' (masculin) ?
quiz.explication: 'du' est l'article partitif masculin singulier.

lecons.contenu:
Textes informatifs, explicatifs et descriptifs : brouillon et révision de l'unité Occupation

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Utiliser une grille d'évaluation pour améliorer la production d'un texte informatif (1er jet, 2e jet)
  • Réviser les articles partitifs (du, de la, de l', des)
  • Réviser les adjectifs de nationalité avant l'évaluation de l'unité

À Douala (Page 48), Bikoy révise son texte sur le métier de son père avec la grille d'évaluation, et consolide articles partitifs et adjectifs de nationalité !

lecons.titre: Les premiers explorateurs européens sur la côte du Cameroun, et la végétation du pays
savoirs_faire: Raconter l'arrivée des premiers explorateurs européens sur la côte du Cameroun
Classer les différentes zones de végétation du Cameroun
Respecter les règles à l'école

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla à Douala raconte comment les premiers EXPLORATEURS EUROPÉENS sont arrivés sur la côte du Cameroun, classe les zones de VÉGÉTATION du pays (forêt, savane), puis rappelle les règles à respecter à l'école.
exercices.astuce: Les premiers Européens sont arrivés par la côte, à Douala notamment, avant de s'installer à l'intérieur du pays.

quiz.question: Par où sont arrivés les premiers explorateurs européens au Cameroun ?
quiz.explication: Les premiers explorateurs européens sont arrivés par la côte du Cameroun.

quiz.question: Lequel est une zone de végétation du Cameroun ?
quiz.explication: La forêt est l'une des zones de végétation du Cameroun, avec la savane.

quiz.question: Que doit-on respecter à l'école ?
quiz.explication: On doit respecter les règles et règlements de l'école.

lecons.contenu:
Les premiers explorateurs européens sur la côte du Cameroun, et la végétation du pays

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • L'arrivée des explorateurs européens
  • Les zones de végétation du Cameroun
  • Les règles à l'école

À Douala (Semaine 1, Page 61), Ekwalla découvre les explorateurs européens, la végétation du Cameroun, et les règles de l'école !

lecons.titre: Les Européens sur la côte du Cameroun (suite), le changement climatique, et l'exploitation/la traite d'êtres humains
savoirs_faire: Continuer à raconter la présence des Européens sur la côte du Cameroun
Discuter du changement climatique en classe
Expliquer l'exploitation et la traite d'êtres humains

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog à Douala continue de raconter l'arrivée des Européens, débat en classe du CHANGEMENT CLIMATIQUE, puis apprend ce qu'est l'EXPLOITATION et la TRAITE d'êtres humains, une grave violation des droits humains.
exercices.astuce: L'exploitation et la traite d'êtres humains sont des violations graves des droits humains.

quiz.question: Qu'est-ce que le changement climatique ?
quiz.explication: Le changement climatique est la modification durable du climat de la planète.

quiz.question: Qu'est-ce que la traite d'êtres humains ?
options: Une grave violation des droits humains
quiz.explication: La traite d'êtres humains est une grave violation des droits humains.

quiz.question: Où se déroule un débat de classe sur le climat ?
quiz.explication: Un débat de classe se déroule entre élèves, encadré par l'enseignant.

lecons.contenu:
Les Européens sur la côte du Cameroun (suite), le changement climatique, et l'exploitation/la traite d'êtres humains

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • La présence des Européens sur la côte
  • Le changement climatique
  • L'exploitation et la traite d'êtres humains

À Douala (Semaine 2, Page 61), Ngo Mbog continue son récit sur les Européens, débat du climat, et apprend la gravité de la traite humaine !

lecons.titre: L'annexion allemande du Cameroun, les mesures contre le changement climatique, et les règles dans la communauté
savoirs_faire: Expliquer comment les Allemands ont annexé le Cameroun
Citer des mesures préventives contre le changement climatique
Respecter les règles et règlements de la communauté

exercices.enonce: Bikoy à Douala apprend comment les ALLEMANDS ont annexé le Cameroun, cite des mesures pour lutter contre le changement climatique (planter des arbres), puis rappelle les règles à respecter dans sa communauté et les bonnes manières à table.
exercices.astuce: L'annexion du Cameroun par l'Allemagne a marqué le début de la période coloniale allemande.

quiz.question: Quel pays a annexé le Cameroun avant les autres puissances coloniales ?
quiz.explication: L'Allemagne a été la première puissance à annexer le Cameroun.

quiz.question: Quelle est une mesure préventive contre le changement climatique ?
quiz.explication: Planter des arbres est une mesure préventive efficace contre le changement climatique.

quiz.question: Pourquoi respecter les règles de la communauté ?
options: Pour vivre en harmonie avec les autres
quiz.explication: Respecter les règles de la communauté permet de vivre en harmonie avec les autres.

lecons.contenu:
L'annexion allemande du Cameroun, les mesures contre le changement climatique, et les règles dans la communauté

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • L'annexion allemande du Cameroun
  • Les mesures contre le changement climatique
  • Les règles de la communauté

À Douala (Semaine 3, Page 62), Bikoy apprend l'annexion allemande, les mesures climatiques, et les règles de sa communauté !

lecons.titre: Les contributions allemandes au Cameroun, la démographie, et les droits de l'enfant
savoirs_faire: Citer les contributions et effets de l'occupation allemande au Cameroun
Expliquer les concepts liés à la démographie (taux de natalité, taux de mortalité)
Citer quelques droits de l'enfant

exercices.enonce: Ndombe à Douala cite les contributions des Allemands au Cameroun (routes, bâtiments), apprend les concepts de DÉMOGRAPHIE (taux de natalité, taux de mortalité), puis liste quelques DROITS DE L'ENFANT avant l'évaluation.
exercices.astuce: La démographie étudie la population : sa natalité, sa mortalité, et sa croissance.

quiz.question: Que signifie 'taux de natalité' ?
options: Le nombre de naissances dans une population
Le nombre de décès dans une population
Le nombre d'écoles dans une ville
quiz.explication: Le taux de natalité mesure le nombre de naissances dans une population.

quiz.question: Lequel est un droit de l'enfant ?
options: Le droit de travailler à temps plein très jeune
quiz.explication: Le droit à l'éducation est l'un des droits fondamentaux de l'enfant.

quiz.question: Qu'ont laissé les Allemands au Cameroun ?
quiz.explication: L'occupation allemande a laissé des contributions comme des routes et bâtiments.

lecons.contenu:
Les contributions allemandes au Cameroun, la démographie, et les droits de l'enfant

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Les contributions allemandes au Cameroun
  • Les concepts de démographie
  • Les droits de l'enfant

À Douala (Semaine 4, Page 62), Ndombe cite les contributions allemandes, apprend la démographie, et liste les droits de l'enfant !

lecons.titre: Creating and Naming Folders
savoirs_faire: Create folders to organize files
Name and rename folders appropriately
Show love for proper organisation

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's father, a clerk in Douala, creates a folder called 'Reports2026' on his computer to keep his work organised, then renames an old folder from 'Docs' to 'OldDocs'.
exercices.astuce: A folder stores related files together. Giving folders clear names helps you find your work quickly. You can rename a folder at any time.

quiz.question: What is a folder used for on a computer?
options: To organize and store related files
quiz.explication: A folder groups related files together for organisation.

quiz.question: Why is it important to give folders clear names?
quiz.explication: Clear folder names help you locate your files quickly.

quiz.question: Can a folder be renamed after it is created?
quiz.explication: Folders can be renamed at any time to keep things organised.

lecons.contenu:
Creating and Naming Folders

What you will learn:

  • Create folders to organize files
  • Name and rename folders appropriately
  • Show love for proper organisation

At his father's office in Douala (Level III syllabus, ICT), Ekwalla learns how office workers create and name folders to stay organised.

lecons.titre: Saving, Searching and Retrieving Files
savoirs_faire: Save a document into the correct folder
Browse to search for folders and files
Retrieve stored information when needed

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog saves her homework as a file inside her 'Homework' folder, then later browses her computer to search for it and retrieve it before printing.
exercices.astuce: Saving a file keeps your work stored. Browsing means looking through folders to find something. Retrieving means opening a file you saved earlier.

quiz.question: What does 'saving' a file mean?
options: Storing your work on the computer
quiz.explication: Saving stores your work so you can find it again later.

quiz.question: What does 'browsing' mean when looking for a file?
options: Looking through folders to find something
quiz.explication: Browsing means looking through folders and files to find what you need.

quiz.question: What does 'retrieving' a file mean?
options: Opening a file you saved earlier
quiz.explication: Retrieving means opening and accessing a file that was saved before.

lecons.contenu:
Saving, Searching and Retrieving Files

What you will learn:

  • Save a document into the correct folder
  • Browse to search for folders and files
  • Retrieve stored information when needed

Doing her homework at home in Douala (Level III syllabus, ICT), Ngo Mbog practises saving, browsing for, and retrieving her files.

lecons.titre: Formatting: Page Layout and Printing
savoirs_faire: Set page layout (portrait and landscape)
Format a document for printing
Show love for aesthetics in document presentation

exercices.enonce: Bikoy prepares a poster in portrait layout (tall) and a certificate in landscape layout (wide), then formats the page before sending it to the printer.
exercices.astuce: Portrait layout is taller than wide, good for letters and posters. Landscape layout is wider than tall, good for certificates and wide tables. Formatting makes a document look neat before printing.

quiz.question: Which page layout is taller than it is wide?
quiz.explication: Portrait layout is taller than it is wide.

quiz.question: Which page layout is wider than it is tall, often used for certificates?
quiz.explication: Landscape layout is wider than it is tall.

quiz.question: Why do we format a document before printing?
options: To make it look neat and organised
To make it slower to print
quiz.explication: Formatting makes a document look neat and professional before printing.

lecons.contenu:
Formatting: Page Layout and Printing

What you will learn:

  • Set page layout (portrait and landscape)
  • Format a document for printing
  • Show love for aesthetics in document presentation

Preparing school materials in Douala (Level III syllabus, ICT), Bikoy formats documents in the correct page layout before printing.

lecons.titre: Word Processing: Typing, Tables and Formatting
savoirs_faire: Type and format a document in a word processor
Insert and use tables in a document
Manifest love for correct spelling and grammar

exercices.enonce: Ndombe types a class list in a word processor, inserts a table to organise names and marks, and uses spelling check to correct her mistakes before showing her teacher.
exercices.astuce: Word processing software is used for typing documents. Tables organise information into rows and columns. Spelling and grammar checks help correct mistakes.

quiz.question: What is a table used for in a document?
options: To organise information into rows and columns
quiz.explication: A table organises information neatly into rows and columns.

quiz.question: What tool helps you correct mistakes while typing?
quiz.explication: Spelling and grammar check tools help correct writing mistakes.

quiz.question: What kind of software is used to type and format documents?
quiz.explication: Word processing software (like Word) is used to type and format documents.

lecons.contenu:
Word Processing: Typing, Tables and Formatting

What you will learn:

  • Type and format a document in a word processor
  • Insert and use tables in a document
  • Manifest love for correct spelling and grammar

Preparing a class list in Douala (Level III syllabus, ICT), Ndombe practises typing, using tables, and checking her spelling.

lecons.titre: Prepositions of Location, Prepositions of Direction, Reading Pictures and Texts, and Informal Letters
savoirs_faire: Identify and use prepositions of location appropriately (in, on, under)
Identify and use prepositions of direction appropriately (to, from, into)
Interpret and appreciate pictures and texts, and write an informal letter

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala shows prepositions of location ('The bag is UNDER the seat') and direction ('We travelled FROM Douala TO Yaoundé'). Ekwalla then studies a picture of a bus station and writes an informal letter to a cousin about the trip.
exercices.astuce: Prepositions of location show where something is (under, on, in); prepositions of direction show movement (to, from, into).

quiz.question: Which word is a preposition of location?
quiz.explication: 'Under' is a preposition of location, showing where something is.

quiz.question: Which word is a preposition of direction?
quiz.explication: 'To' is a preposition of direction, showing movement toward a place.

quiz.question: What kind of letter is written this week?
quiz.explication: An informal letter, like one written to a family member, is written this week.

lecons.contenu:
Prepositions of Location, Prepositions of Direction, Reading Pictures and Texts, and Informal Letters

What you will learn:

  • Use prepositions of location
  • Use prepositions of direction
  • Read pictures/texts and write an informal letter

In Douala (Week 1, Page 11), Ekwalla learns prepositions of location and direction, and writes an informal letter!

lecons.titre: Prepositions of Time and Relationship, Possessive Pronouns, Reading Comprehension, and Informal Letters
savoirs_faire: Identify and use prepositions of time and relationship (before, after, with)
Identify and use possessive pronouns (mine, yours, hers)
Read comprehension speeches, and continue writing informal letters

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog's teacher in Douala shows prepositions of time ('We left BEFORE sunrise') and possessive pronouns ('That seat is MINE'). Ngo Mbog then reads a speech about travel safety and continues an informal letter about the weather during the trip.
exercices.astuce: Possessive pronouns (mine, yours, hers) replace a noun to show ownership without repeating it.

quiz.question: Which word is a preposition of time?
quiz.explication: 'Before' is a preposition of time, showing when something happens.

quiz.question: Which word is a possessive pronoun?
quiz.explication: 'Mine' is a possessive pronoun, showing ownership.

quiz.question: What do pupils read this week?
quiz.explication: A comprehension speech is read this week.

lecons.contenu:
Prepositions of Time and Relationship, Possessive Pronouns, Reading Comprehension, and Informal Letters

What you will learn:

  • Use prepositions of time and relationship
  • Use possessive pronouns
  • Read a speech and continue an informal letter

In Douala (Week 2, Page 11), Ngo Mbog learns prepositions of time and possessive pronouns!

lecons.titre: Subject Pronouns, Reading Comprehension: Short Stories, and Formal Letters
savoirs_faire: Use subject pronouns appropriately (I, you, he, she, it, we, they)
Read comprehension short stories about travel
Write a formal letter correctly

exercices.enonce: Bikoy's teacher in Douala shows subject pronouns: 'SHE travelled by bus, THEY travelled by train.' Bikoy then reads a short story about a family trip, and writes a formal letter requesting travel information from a bus company.
exercices.astuce: Subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they) replace the subject noun in a sentence.

quiz.question: Which of these is a subject pronoun?
quiz.explication: 'She' is a subject pronoun, replacing a subject noun.

quiz.question: What type of letter is written this week?
quiz.explication: A formal letter, such as one requesting information, is written this week.

quiz.question: What do pupils read about this week?
quiz.explication: A short story about a family trip is read this week.

lecons.contenu:
Subject Pronouns, Reading Comprehension: Short Stories, and Formal Letters

What you will learn:

  • Use subject pronouns
  • Read a short story about travel
  • Write a formal letter

In Douala (Week 3, Page 12), Bikoy learns subject pronouns and writes a formal letter!

lecons.titre: Subject Pronouns Continued, Reading Short Stories, and November Integration
savoirs_faire: Continue using subject pronouns correctly
Read comprehension short stories fluently
Complete integration activities, evaluation and remediation

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala reviews subject pronouns with more travel sentences: 'WE arrived late, IT was raining.' Ekwalla then finishes reading a short story before completing this month's integration and evaluation.
exercices.astuce: Reviewing subject pronouns with real sentences helps them stick in memory.

quiz.question: In 'WE arrived late', what type of word is 'WE'?
quiz.explication: 'WE' is a subject pronoun.

quiz.question: What is read fluently this week?
quiz.explication: A short story is read fluently this week.

quiz.question: What happens during integration week?
options: Applying the month's lessons and completing evaluation
quiz.explication: Integration weeks apply the month's lessons and include evaluation and remediation.

lecons.contenu:
Subject Pronouns Continued, Reading Short Stories, and November Integration

What you will learn:

  • Continue using subject pronouns
  • Read a short story fluently
  • Complete this month's integration and evaluation

In Douala (Week 4, Page 12), Ekwalla reviews subject pronouns and completes November integration!

lecons.titre: Significant Figures, Converting Fractions, and Calculating Time
savoirs_faire: Write numbers to a given number of significant figures
Convert fractions from mixed to improper numbers and vice versa, and reduce fractions to their simplest term
Convert fractions to decimals and vice versa, and calculate time

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala rounds '3,847' to 2 significant figures: '3,800'. Ekwalla converts the mixed fraction '2 1/2' to the improper fraction '5/2', reduces '6/8' to '3/4', and calculates a journey time of '2 hours 30 minutes'.
exercices.astuce: A mixed fraction has a whole number and a fraction together (e.g. 2 1/2); an improper fraction has a numerator larger than its denominator (e.g. 5/2).

quiz.question: What is 3,847 rounded to 2 significant figures?
quiz.explication: Rounding 3,847 to 2 significant figures gives 3,800.

quiz.question: What is the improper fraction form of 2 1/2 ?
What is 6/8 reduced to its simplest term?
quiz.explication: 6/8 simplifies to 3/4 by dividing numerator and denominator by 2.

lecons.contenu:
Significant Figures, Converting Fractions, and Calculating Time

What you will learn:

  • Write numbers to a given number of significant figures
  • Convert fractions from mixed to improper numbers and vice versa, and reduce fractions to their simplest term
  • Convert fractions to decimals and vice versa, and calculate time

In Douala (Week 1, Page 27), Ekwalla rounds significant figures, converts fractions, and calculates journey time for a trip!

lecons.titre: Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication and Division of Fractions
savoirs_faire: Add and subtract fractions with the same and different denominators
Multiply and divide fractions
Simplify decimal fractions to their lowest term

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog's teacher in Douala adds '1/4 + 1/2 = 3/4' while packing for a trip. Ngo Mbog multiplies '2/3 × 3/5 = 6/15 = 2/5', divides '1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 2', and simplifies '4/8' to '1/2'.
exercices.astuce: To add or subtract fractions, first find a common denominator. To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal.

quiz.question: What is 1/4 + 1/2 ?
What is 2/3 × 3/5 ?
quiz.explication: 2/3 × 3/5 = 6/15, which simplifies to 2/5.

quiz.question: What is 1/2 ÷ 1/4 ?
quiz.explication: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 1/2 × 4/1 = 2.

lecons.contenu:
Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication and Division of Fractions

What you will learn:

  • Add and subtract fractions with the same and different denominators
  • Multiply and divide fractions
  • Simplify decimal fractions to their lowest term

In Douala (Week 2, Page 27), Ngo Mbog adds, multiplies and divides fractions while packing for a journey!

lecons.titre: BODMAS, Significant Figures, Rounding Decimals, and Area of a Trapezium
savoirs_faire: Solve problems involving BODMAS (order of operations)
Write numbers to a given significant figure, and round up decimal numbers to a given number of decimal places
Find the area of a trapezium, and present information on a bar chart

exercices.enonce: Bikoy's teacher in Douala solves '(4 + 6) × 2 = 20' using BODMAS (Brackets first). Bikoy rounds '7.368' to 2 decimal places: '7.37', and finds the area of a trapezium for a travel poster: parallel sides 5 cm and 9 cm, height 3 cm, Area = 21 cm².
exercices.astuce: BODMAS order: Brackets, Orders (powers), Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

quiz.question: Using BODMAS, what is (4 + 6) × 2 ?
quiz.explication: Brackets first: (4+6)=10, then 10×2=20.

quiz.question: What is 7.368 rounded to 2 decimal places?
quiz.explication: 7.368 rounds to 7.37 at 2 decimal places.

quiz.question: What does the 'B' in BODMAS stand for?
quiz.explication: BODMAS starts with Brackets, solved first.

lecons.contenu:
BODMAS, Significant Figures, Rounding Decimals, and Area of a Trapezium

What you will learn:

  • Solve problems involving BODMAS (order of operations)
  • Write numbers to a given significant figure, and round up decimal numbers to a given number of decimal places
  • Find the area of a trapezium, and present information on a bar chart

In Douala (Week 3, Page 27-28), Bikoy applies BODMAS, rounds decimals, and calculates a trapezium's area for a travel poster!

lecons.titre: Number Bases: Addition, Subtraction, and Conversion
savoirs_faire: Add and subtract numbers in a given base
Convert numbers from base 10 to other bases
Convert numbers from other bases to base 10

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala converts '13' (base 10) to base 2: '1101'. Ekwalla adds numbers in base 2: '101 + 110 = 1011', and converts '1010' (base 2) back to base 10: '10'.
exercices.astuce: To convert base 10 to another base, divide repeatedly by the new base and record the remainders. To convert to base 10, multiply each digit by the base raised to its position power.

quiz.question: What is 13 (base 10) converted to base 2?
What is 1010 (base 2) converted to base 10?
Which base uses only the digits 0 and 1?
quiz.explication: Base 2, or binary, uses only 0 and 1.

lecons.contenu:
Number Bases: Addition, Subtraction, and Conversion

What you will learn:

  • Add and subtract numbers in a given base
  • Convert numbers from base 10 to other bases
  • Convert numbers from other bases to base 10

In Douala (Week 4, Page 28), Ekwalla converts numbers between base 10 and base 2, and adds numbers in binary!

lecons.titre: Types of Toilets, Types of Insects, and Electrical Devices
savoirs_faire: State and explain types of toilets (pit latrine, water closet)
Identify different types of insects (ants, bees, mosquitoes, flies)
Identify electrical devices (bulb, fan, iron, radio)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala names types of toilets: pit latrine and water closet. Ekwalla then identifies insects in the school garden like ants and bees, and names electrical devices at home like a bulb and a fan.
exercices.astuce: A pit latrine and a water closet are common types of toilets.

quiz.question: Which of these is a type of toilet?
quiz.explication: A pit latrine and a water closet are common types of toilets.

quiz.question: Which of these is an insect?
quiz.explication: An ant is a small insect with six legs.

quiz.question: Which of these is an electrical device?
quiz.explication: An electric bulb runs on electricity.

lecons.contenu:
Types of Toilets, Types of Insects, and Electrical Devices

What you will learn:

  • Learn types of toilets
  • Identify types of insects
  • Identify electrical devices

In Douala (Week 1, Page 35), Ekwalla names types of toilets, identifies insects, and names electrical devices!

lecons.titre: Usage and Ethics of Toilets, the Mode of Reproduction of Insects, and the Uses of Electricity
savoirs_faire: State and explain the responsible usage and ethics of toilets
Explain the mode of reproduction of insects (laying eggs)
State and discuss the uses of electricity (lighting, cooking, powering devices)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains that using toilets responsibly means flushing after use and keeping them clean for others. Ekwalla then learns that most insects reproduce by laying eggs, and names uses of electricity like lighting and cooking.
exercices.astuce: Using toilets responsibly means flushing after use and keeping them clean for the next person.

quiz.question: What does using a toilet responsibly mean?
options: Flushing after use and keeping it clean
quiz.explication: Using a toilet responsibly means flushing after use and keeping it clean for others.

quiz.question: How do most insects reproduce?
quiz.explication: Most insects reproduce by laying eggs.

quiz.question: Which of these is a use of electricity?
quiz.explication: Electricity is used for lighting, cooking, and powering many devices.

lecons.contenu:
Usage and Ethics of Toilets, the Mode of Reproduction of Insects, and the Uses of Electricity

What you will learn:

  • Learn responsible toilet usage and ethics
  • Learn how insects reproduce
  • Discuss the uses of electricity

In Douala (Week 2, Page 35), Ekwalla learns toilet ethics, insect reproduction, and uses of electricity!

lecons.titre: Care of Toilets, Social Insects and Their Importance, and the Dangers of Electricity
savoirs_faire: Discuss the care of toilets and clean toilets using appropriate materials
Explain the activities of social insects (bees, ants, termites) and their importance
Explain the dangers and safety measures of electricity

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains that cleaning a toilet regularly with soap and water prevents disease. Ekwalla then learns that bees work together in colonies to make honey, and reviews electricity dangers like electric shock and how to avoid them.
exercices.astuce: Social insects like bees live and work together in organized colonies.

quiz.question: What should be used to clean a toilet?
quiz.explication: Cleaning a toilet with soap and water regularly prevents disease.

quiz.question: What is a social insect?
options: An insect that lives and works in organized colonies
An insect that lives completely alone always
quiz.explication: Social insects like bees, ants, and termites live and work together in colonies.

quiz.question: What is a danger of electricity?
quiz.explication: Electric shock is a danger associated with improper use of electricity.

lecons.contenu:
Care of Toilets, Social Insects and Their Importance, and the Dangers of Electricity

What you will learn:

  • Learn how to care for toilets
  • Learn about social insects
  • Learn the dangers of electricity

In Douala (Week 3, Page 35), Ekwalla learns toilet care, social insects, and electricity dangers!

lecons.titre: The Importance of Toilets, Characteristics and Usefulness of Insects, and Electricity Wiring
savoirs_faire: State and discuss the importance of toilets
Describe the characteristics and usefulness of insects
Describe how to install electricity (basic wiring)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's teacher in Douala explains that toilets protect health by keeping waste away from living areas. Ekwalla then describes insect characteristics (six legs, small body) and their usefulness (pollination), and watches an electrician install a wire safely.
exercices.astuce: Toilets are important because they protect health by keeping human waste away from living and eating areas.

quiz.question: Why are toilets important?
options: They protect health by keeping waste away from living areas
quiz.explication: Toilets protect health by keeping human waste away from living and eating areas.

quiz.question: What are common characteristics of insects?
options: Six legs and a small body
quiz.explication: Insects generally have six legs and a small body divided into parts.

quiz.question: Who should install electrical wiring?
quiz.explication: Electrical wiring should be installed by a trained electrician for safety.

lecons.contenu:
The Importance of Toilets, Characteristics and Usefulness of Insects, and Electricity Wiring

What you will learn:

  • Discuss the importance of toilets
  • Describe insect characteristics and usefulness
  • Learn about electricity wiring

In Douala (Week 4, Page 35), Ekwalla learns the importance of toilets, insect characteristics, and electricity wiring!

lecons.titre: L'imparfait de l'indicatif et réorganiser un texte en désordre
savoirs_faire: Identifier et utiliser correctement l'imparfait de l'indicatif dans un récit de voyage
Réorganiser les paragraphes d'un texte en désordre (6 à 8 lignes)
Reconnaître les terminaisons de l'imparfait (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient)

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla à Douala raconte : 'Chaque année, nous VOYAGIONS à Kribi. Mon père CONDUISAIT la voiture et ma mère PRÉPARAIT le repas.' Puis il remet dans l'ordre un texte de voyage mélangé.
exercices.astuce: L'imparfait décrit une action habituelle ou en cours dans le passé. Terminaisons : -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.

quiz.question: Quelle est la terminaison de l'imparfait avec 'nous' ?
quiz.explication: 'nous' prend -ions à l'imparfait.

quiz.question: Quand utilise-t-on l'imparfait ?
options: Pour une action habituelle ou en cours dans le passé
quiz.explication: L'imparfait décrit une action habituelle ou en cours dans le passé.

quiz.question: Que faut-il faire face à un texte en désordre ?
options: Réorganiser les paragraphes dans un ordre cohérent
quiz.explication: Il faut réorganiser les paragraphes mélangés dans un ordre logique.

lecons.contenu:
L'imparfait de l'indicatif et réorganiser un texte en désordre

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Identifier et utiliser correctement l'imparfait de l'indicatif dans un récit de voyage
  • Réorganiser les paragraphes d'un texte en désordre (6 à 8 lignes)
  • Reconnaître les terminaisons de l'imparfait (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient)

À Douala (Semaine 1, Page 49), Ekwalla raconte ses voyages à l'imparfait (nous voyagions, il conduisait), et réorganise un texte en désordre !

lecons.titre: Concordance des temps (imparfait et passé composé) et accord sujet-verbe
savoirs_faire: Identifier et utiliser correctement la concordance entre l'imparfait et le passé composé
Accorder correctement le sujet et le verbe dans une phrase
Distinguer l'action de fond (imparfait) de l'action ponctuelle (passé composé)

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog à Douala écrit : 'Nous ÉTIONS en route (imparfait, action de fond) quand la pluie A COMMENCÉ (passé composé, action ponctuelle).' Elle vérifie l'accord : 'Les voyageurs ARRIVENT.'
exercices.astuce: L'imparfait pose le décor (action de fond) ; le passé composé marque l'action précise qui interrompt. Le verbe s'accorde toujours avec son sujet.

quiz.question: Dans 'Nous étions en route quand la pluie a commencé', quel temps marque l'action ponctuelle ?
quiz.explication: Le passé composé marque l'action ponctuelle qui interrompt l'action de fond.

quiz.question: Avec quoi le verbe s'accorde-t-il toujours ?
quiz.explication: Le verbe s'accorde en personne et en nombre avec son sujet.

quiz.question: Quel temps pose le décor ou l'action habituelle dans un récit ?
quiz.explication: L'imparfait pose le décor et les actions habituelles.

lecons.contenu:
Concordance des temps (imparfait et passé composé) et accord sujet-verbe

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Identifier et utiliser correctement la concordance entre l'imparfait et le passé composé
  • Accorder correctement le sujet et le verbe dans une phrase
  • Distinguer l'action de fond (imparfait) de l'action ponctuelle (passé composé)

À Douala (Semaine 2, Page 49), Ngo Mbog apprend la concordance imparfait/passé composé, et vérifie l'accord sujet-verbe pendant son récit de voyage !

lecons.titre: Les homophones grammaticaux et les graphies des phonèmes (ph/f, eau/ô)
savoirs_faire: Utiliser correctement les homophones grammaticaux de base (ou/où, on/ont, est/et, à/as/a)
Identifier et écrire correctement les graphies du phonème [f] (ph, f) et [o] (o, eau, ô)
Accorder correctement les participes passés dans un texte de voyage

exercices.enonce: Bikoy à Douala écrit : 'OÙ vas-tu ? À la gare OU à l'aéroport ?' Il note aussi 'un ÉLÉPHANT' (graphie ph=[f]) et 'un BATEAU' (graphie eau=[o]) pour son carnet de voyage.
exercices.astuce: 'où' avec accent indique le lieu ; 'ou' sans accent est une conjonction de choix. Le son [f] peut s'écrire 'f' ou 'ph' ; le son [o] peut s'écrire 'o', 'eau' ou 'ô'.

quiz.question: Quel homophone indique le LIEU dans 'La ville ___ j'habite' ?
quiz.explication: 'où' avec accent grave indique le lieu.

quiz.question: Comment s'écrit le son [f] dans le mot 'éléphant' ?
quiz.explication: Dans 'éléphant', le son [f] s'écrit 'ph'.

quiz.question: Quelle est la bonne orthographe du participe passé dans 'Les valises sont ___ (préparer)' ?
quiz.explication: Avec l'auxiliaire être, le participe passé s'accorde avec le sujet féminin pluriel 'les valises'.

lecons.contenu:
Les homophones grammaticaux et les graphies des phonèmes (ph/f, eau/ô)

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Utiliser correctement les homophones grammaticaux de base (ou/où, on/ont, est/et, à/as/a)
  • Identifier et écrire correctement les graphies du phonème [f] (ph, f) et [o] (o, eau, ô)
  • Accorder correctement les participes passés dans un texte de voyage

À Douala (Page 50), Bikoy distingue les homophones (où/ou), les graphies du son [f] (ph) et [o] (eau), et accorde les participes passés de son carnet de voyage !

lecons.titre: Physical Geography of Africa: Continents, Oceans and Mountains
savoirs_faire: Label major continents and oceans of the world
Identify major mountains, seas and rivers of Africa
Show interest in the physical geography of the world

exercices.enonce: Before their family trip, Ngo Mbog studies a map of Africa with her father: the Atlantic and Indian Oceans border the continent, Mount Cameroon rises near Douala, and great rivers like the Congo and the Nile flow across the land.
exercices.astuce: The world has seven continents and several oceans. Africa has major mountains (like Mount Cameroon and Kilimanjaro), seas, and rivers (like the Congo and the Nile).

quiz.question: Which ocean borders the west coast of Cameroon?
quiz.explication: The Atlantic Ocean borders the west coast of Cameroon.

quiz.question: What is the name of the mountain near Douala?
quiz.explication: Mount Cameroon is the well-known mountain near Douala.

quiz.question: Which major river flows through Central Africa?
quiz.explication: The Congo River is a major river flowing through Central Africa.

lecons.contenu:
Physical Geography of Africa: Continents, Oceans and Mountains

What you will learn:

  • Label major continents and oceans of the world
  • Identify major mountains, seas and rivers of Africa
  • Show interest in the physical geography of the world

Planning a family trip from Douala (Level III syllabus, Geography: Physical Geography), Ngo Mbog studies Africa's continents, oceans and mountains.

lecons.titre: Reading Maps and Using GPS for Travel
savoirs_faire: Draw and read simple maps of Cameroon
Use a Global Positioning System (GPS) to locate places
Follow directions and locate places on a map

exercices.enonce: Before a road trip to Kribi, Bikoy's family uses a GPS app on their phone to follow directions, while Bikoy also traces their route on a paper map of Cameroon's regions.
exercices.astuce: Maps show places and their locations. A GPS (Global Positioning System) uses satellites to help travellers find their way and follow directions.

quiz.question: What does GPS stand for?
quiz.explication: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.

quiz.question: What does a GPS use to help travellers find their way?
quiz.explication: GPS uses satellites to determine location and give directions.

quiz.question: What tool can also be used alongside GPS to trace a travel route?
quiz.explication: A paper map can be used alongside GPS to trace a travel route.

lecons.contenu:
Reading Maps and Using GPS for Travel

What you will learn:

  • Draw and read simple maps of Cameroon
  • Use a Global Positioning System (GPS) to locate places
  • Follow directions and locate places on a map

Preparing for a road trip from Douala to Kribi (Level III syllabus, Geography: Plans and Maps), Bikoy learns to read maps and use GPS.

lecons.titre: Population, Settlements and Migration
savoirs_faire: Explain population concepts (birth rate, death rate)
Differentiate between rural and urban settlements
Describe migration and its causes

exercices.enonce: Travelling from their rural village to Douala, a big urban city, Ndombe's family discusses why people migrate: some move to cities for jobs and schools, changing the population of both places.
exercices.astuce: Population growth is related to birth rate and death rate. Settlements can be rural (villages) or urban (cities). Migration is when people move from one place to another, often for work or opportunities.

quiz.question: What is the difference between a rural and an urban settlement?
options: Rural is village-like, urban is city-like
quiz.explication: Rural settlements are village-like with fewer people; urban settlements are city-like with more people.

quiz.question: What is 'migration'?
options: People moving from one place to another
quiz.explication: Migration is the movement of people from one place to another.

quiz.question: Why do people often migrate to cities?
quiz.explication: People often migrate to cities seeking jobs, schools and better opportunities.

lecons.contenu:
Population, Settlements and Migration

What you will learn:

  • Explain population concepts (birth rate, death rate)
  • Differentiate between rural and urban settlements
  • Describe migration and its causes

Travelling from a village to Douala (Level III syllabus, Geography: Population), Ndombe learns about settlements and migration.

lecons.titre: Economic Activities: Agriculture, Transportation and Trade
savoirs_faire: Identify economic and human activities (agriculture, transportation, trade)
Explain the importance of transportation for travel and trade
Show interest in entrepreneurship and self-reliance

exercices.enonce: On their journey, Ekwalla's family passes farms (agriculture), buses and trains (transportation), and busy markets (trade) — all economic activities that connect people and places across Cameroon.
exercices.astuce: Agriculture produces food and goods, transportation moves people and goods between places, and trade is the exchange of goods and services. Together, they support travel and the economy.

quiz.question: What economic activity involves growing crops and raising animals?
quiz.explication: Agriculture involves growing crops and raising animals.

quiz.question: What economic activity moves people and goods between places?
quiz.explication: Transportation moves people and goods between places.

quiz.question: What is 'trade'?
options: The exchange of goods and services
quiz.explication: Trade is the exchange of goods and services between people.

lecons.contenu:
Economic Activities: Agriculture, Transportation and Trade

What you will learn:

  • Identify economic and human activities (agriculture, transportation, trade)
  • Explain the importance of transportation for travel and trade
  • Show interest in entrepreneurship and self-reliance

Travelling across Cameroon from Douala (Level III syllabus, Geography: Economic Activities), Ekwalla observes agriculture, transportation and trade.

lecons.titre: PowerPoint: Creating Slides
savoirs_faire: Create slides for a PowerPoint presentation
Insert items (text and images) in a slide
Time a slide show

exercices.enonce: Before her family trip, Ekwalla's cousin creates a PowerPoint presentation about Cameroon's regions, with one slide per destination, inserting pictures and short text on each.
exercices.astuce: PowerPoint is used to create slide presentations. Each slide can contain text, images and other items. A slide show can be timed to move automatically.

quiz.question: What software is used to create slide presentations?
quiz.explication: PowerPoint is used to create slide presentations.

quiz.question: What can you insert into a PowerPoint slide?
quiz.explication: Slides can contain text, images, and other items.

quiz.question: What does 'timing a slide show' mean?
options: Setting slides to move automatically after a set time
quiz.explication: Timing a slide show sets each slide to advance automatically after a chosen duration.

lecons.contenu:

quiz.question: Why is it important to respect other people's privacy online?

In Douala (Week 2, Page 15), Ngo Mbog learns interjections of grief, sentence types, and writes a persuasive essay!

lecons.titre: Types of Angles & Parallel/Intersecting Lines
savoirs_faire: Identify right, acute and obtuse angles
Differentiate between parallel and intersecting lines
Draw curves and lines using real objects

exercices.enonce: During games time in Douala, Ekwalla measures the corner of the football goal post: it forms a right angle (90°). Bikoy notices the two touchlines of the field never meet: they are parallel lines. Where the touchline meets the goal line, the lines intersect.
exercices.astuce: A right angle is exactly 90°. An acute angle is less than 90°, an obtuse angle is more than 90°. Parallel lines never meet; intersecting lines cross at a point.

quiz.question: What is an angle of exactly 90° called?
quiz.explication: A right angle measures exactly 90°, like the corner of a goal post.

quiz.question: What do we call lines that never meet, like the touchlines of a football field?
quiz.explication: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet.

quiz.question: An angle smaller than 90° is called what?
quiz.explication: An acute angle is less than 90°; an obtuse angle is more than 90°.

lecons.contenu:
Types of Angles & Parallel/Intersecting Lines

What you will learn:

  • Identify right, acute and obtuse angles
  • Differentiate between parallel and intersecting lines
  • Draw curves and lines using real objects

At the Douala sports ground (Level III syllabus, Geometry), Ekwalla and Bikoy explore angles and lines on the football field before their game.

lecons.titre: 2D Shapes: Triangles, Quadrilaterals, Pentagon & Hexagon
savoirs_faire: Identify types of triangles (right, isosceles, equilateral, scalene)
Identify quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, trapezium, parallelogram)
Recognize pentagons and hexagons

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog draws the shapes she sees at the sports competition in Douala: the corner flag is a triangle, the field is a rectangle, and the referee's badge is a pentagon (5 sides). Ndombe finds a hexagon (6 sides) on a football design.
exercices.astuce: A triangle has 3 sides. A quadrilateral has 4 sides (square, rectangle, trapezium, parallelogram). A pentagon has 5 sides, a hexagon has 6 sides.

quiz.question: How many sides does a pentagon have?
quiz.explication: A pentagon has 5 sides, like the referee's badge Ngo Mbog saw.

quiz.question: A triangle with all three sides equal is called what?
quiz.explication: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides. An isosceles triangle has 2 equal sides. A scalene triangle has no equal sides.

quiz.question: How many sides does a hexagon have?
quiz.explication: A hexagon has 6 sides, like the pattern Ndombe found on the football.

lecons.contenu:
2D Shapes: Triangles, Quadrilaterals, Pentagon & Hexagon

lecons.titre: 3D Shapes: Cylinder, Cone, Sphere, Cube & Prism

exercices.enonce: At the games ground, Bikoy identifies: the football is a sphere, the water bottle is a cylinder, the tent used for shade is shaped like a cone and a prism, and the equipment box is a cube.
exercices.astuce: A sphere is perfectly round (like a ball). A cylinder has two flat circular ends. A cone narrows to a point. A cube has 6 equal square faces. Volume measures how much space a 3D shape takes up.

quiz.question: What 3D shape is a football?
quiz.explication: A football is round in every direction: a sphere.

quiz.question: Which 3D shape has 6 equal square faces?
quiz.explication: A cube has 6 equal square faces, like the equipment box.

quiz.question: What 3D shape narrows to a single point at the top?

3D Shapes: Cylinder, Cone, Sphere, Cube & Prism

exercices.astuce: A protractor measures angles in degrees. To read it, line up the base with one side of the angle and read where the other side crosses the scale. A pattern repeats in a predictable order.

quiz.question: What tool is used to measure an angle in degrees?
quiz.explication: A protractor measures angles in degrees.

quiz.question: In the pattern red, blue, red, blue, red... what comes next?
quiz.explication: The pattern alternates red, blue — after red comes blue.

quiz.question: If a protractor shows 45°, is this angle acute, right, or obtuse?
quiz.explication: 45° is less than 90°, so it is acute.

lecons.contenu:
Measuring Angles with a Protractor & Patterns

What you will learn:

  • Measure angles using a protractor
  • Complete and continue mathematical patterns
  • Construct simple geometric models

On the athletics track in Douala (Level III syllabus, Geometry), Ekwalla and Ngo Mbog practice using a protractor and spotting patterns among the games equipment.

quiz.question: What is water in its liquid state?

quiz.question: Why should safety measures be applied during sports?
quiz.explication: Safety measures during sports help prevent injuries.

Exprimer l'obligation : je dois, je ne dois pas, il faut, il ne faut pas

quiz.question: Comment exprime-t-on une obligation en français ?
quiz.explication: L'obligation s'exprime avec 'je dois' ou 'il faut' suivi d'un infinitif.

lecons.contenu:

lecons.titre: Les conjonctions de coordination et de subordination, et les adverbes
savoirs_faire: Utiliser correctement les conjonctions de coordination et de subordination dans une phrase complexe
Utiliser correctement les adverbes dans un énoncé
Lire silencieusement et à voix haute des textes variés de 8 à 10 phrases

exercices.astuce: Les conjonctions de coordination (mais, ou, et, donc, or, ni, car) relient deux propositions. Les conjonctions de subordination (parce que, quand, si) introduisent une proposition dépendante.

quiz.question: Laquelle de ces conjonctions est une conjonction de coordination ?
quiz.explication: 'mais' est une conjonction de coordination.

quiz.question: Laquelle de ces conjonctions est une conjonction de subordination ?
quiz.explication: 'parce que' introduit une proposition subordonnée de cause.

quiz.question: Quelle est la fonction d'un adverbe comme 'rapidement' ?
quiz.explication: L'adverbe 'rapidement' modifie le verbe 'nager'.

lecons.contenu:
Les conjonctions de coordination et de subordination, et les adverbes

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Utiliser correctement les conjonctions de coordination et de subordination dans une phrase complexe
  • Utiliser correctement les adverbes dans un énoncé
  • Lire silencieusement et à voix haute des textes variés de 8 à 10 phrases

À Douala (Semaine 2, Page 54), Ngo Mbog utilise les conjonctions de coordination et de subordination, et les adverbes en parlant de sport !

lecons.titre: Les indicateurs du passé et les compléments d'objet direct et indirect (COD, COI)
savoirs_faire: Identifier et utiliser correctement les indicateurs du passé (en..., à..., depuis, pendant, hier)
Identifier les compléments d'objet direct (COD) et indirect (COI) dans une phrase
Identifier les aspects importants de la structure d'un texte narratif (affiche, lettre, dialogue)

exercices.enonce: Bikoy à Douala raconte : 'HIER, j'ai joué au football PENDANT deux heures.' Il analyse : 'Je regarde LE MATCH (COD)' et 'Je parle À MON ÉQUIPE (COI)'.
exercices.astuce: Le COD répond à la question 'quoi/qui' sans préposition ; le COI répond à 'à qui/de quoi' avec une préposition.

quiz.question: Dans 'Je regarde le match', quelle est la fonction de 'le match' ?
quiz.explication: 'le match' répond à 'je regarde quoi ?' sans préposition : c'est un COD.

quiz.question: Dans 'Je parle à mon équipe', quelle est la fonction de 'à mon équipe' ?
quiz.explication: 'à mon équipe' répond à 'je parle à qui ?' avec préposition : c'est un COI.

quiz.question: Lequel de ces mots est un indicateur du passé ?
quiz.explication: 'hier' est un indicateur de temps du passé.

lecons.contenu:
Les indicateurs du passé et les compléments d'objet direct et indirect (COD, COI)

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Identifier et utiliser correctement les indicateurs du passé (en..., à..., depuis, pendant, hier)
  • Identifier les compléments d'objet direct (COD) et indirect (COI) dans une phrase
  • Identifier les aspects importants de la structure d'un texte narratif (affiche, lettre, dialogue)

À Douala (Page 55), Bikoy raconte son match d'hier avec les indicateurs du passé, et identifie les COD et COI !
