quiz.question: Quelle expression permet de demander un chemin ?
quiz.explication: 'Quelle est la route pour...' permet de demander un itinéraire.

quiz.question: Que signifie 'tout droit' dans un itinéraire ?
quiz.explication: 'Tout droit' signifie continuer sans tourner.

lecons.contenu:
Biens et services : demander et dire un prix, demander un itinéraire

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Demander et dire le prix des articles et services (combien y a-t-il, combien ça coûte)
  • Demander et dire un itinéraire simple (à gauche, à droite, tout droit)
  • Réutiliser ce vocabulaire dans un dialogue de la vie courante à Douala

À Douala (Semaine 1, Page 56), Ekwalla demande un prix au marché (combien ça coûte ?) et son chemin pour l'école (tout droit, à gauche) !

lecons.titre: Rédiger une recette et compter de 7 000 à 10 000
savoirs_faire: Rédiger une recette (structure, mode d'emploi, verbes à l'impératif)
Compter et écrire les nombres de 7 000 à 10 000, en chiffres et en lettres
Faire des comptes simples liés aux ingrédients d'une recette

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog à Douala rédige une recette : 'ÉPLUCHEZ les plantains, COUPEZ-les, FAITES-les frire.' Elle calcule le prix des ingrédients : 7 500 francs (sept mille cinq cents francs) pour tout acheter.
exercices.astuce: Une recette utilise l'impératif (épluchez, coupez, faites). Les nombres de 7000 à 10000 s'écrivent avec 'mille' invariable : sept mille, huit mille cinq cents...

quiz.question: À quel mode sont conjugués les verbes d'une recette (épluchez, coupez) ?
quiz.explication: Les recettes utilisent l'impératif pour donner des instructions.

quiz.question: Comment écrit-on 8 500 en lettres ?
quiz.explication: 8 500 s'écrit 'huit mille cinq cents'.

quiz.question: Le mot 'mille' est-il variable ou invariable dans les nombres ?
options: Variable, il prend un -s au pluriel
quiz.explication: 'mille' est toujours invariable : huit mille, neuf mille.

lecons.contenu:
Rédiger une recette et compter de 7 000 à 10 000

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Rédiger une recette (structure, mode d'emploi, verbes à l'impératif)
  • Compter et écrire les nombres de 7 000 à 10 000, en chiffres et en lettres
  • Faire des comptes simples liés aux ingrédients d'une recette

À Douala (Semaine 2, Page 57), Ngo Mbog rédige une recette de plantains frits à l'impératif, et compte les ingrédients jusqu'à 10 000 francs !

lecons.titre: Les conjonctions, les adverbes en -ment, et révision du passé composé
savoirs_faire: Utiliser correctement les conjonctions de coordination et de subordination
Identifier les adverbes en -ment et leur formation
Réviser le champ lexical de la santé, les familles de mots, et le passé composé des verbes des 3 groupes

exercices.enonce: Bikoy à Douala termine l'année : 'J'ai TRAVAILLÉ sérieusement ET j'ai progressé RAPIDEMENT.' Il révise le champ lexical de la santé (médecin, soigner, guérir) et forme des familles de mots (santé, sain, sainement).
exercices.astuce: L'adverbe en -ment se forme souvent à partir de l'adjectif féminin : rapide → rapidement, sérieuse → sérieusement. Le passé composé se forme avec avoir ou être + participe passé.

quiz.question: Comment forme-t-on l'adverbe à partir de l'adjectif 'sérieuse' ?
quiz.explication: On ajoute '-ment' à l'adjectif féminin : sérieuse → sérieusement.

quiz.question: Avec quels auxiliaires forme-t-on le passé composé ?
quiz.explication: Le passé composé se forme avec l'auxiliaire avoir ou être + participe passé.

quiz.question: Lequel de ces mots appartient au champ lexical de la santé ?
quiz.explication: 'soigner' appartient au champ lexical de la santé, comme médecin et guérir.

lecons.contenu:
Les conjonctions, les adverbes en -ment, et révision du passé composé

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Utiliser correctement les conjonctions de coordination et de subordination
  • Identifier les adverbes en -ment et leur formation
  • Réviser le champ lexical de la santé, les familles de mots, et le passé composé des verbes des 3 groupes

À Douala (Page 58), Bikoy révise les conjonctions, les adverbes en -ment, le champ lexical de la santé, et le passé composé pour conclure l'année de Français !

lecons.titre: Independence and Reunification of Cameroon
savoirs_faire: Trace the origin of Cameroon's independence
Explain the reunification of Cameroon
Appreciate the importance of key political figures

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla's grandfather in Douala tells him how Cameroon gained independence and how the French and British Cameroons later reunified to form one country, an important story communicated across generations.
exercices.astuce: Cameroon gained independence and later reunified, joining the formerly French and British administered territories into one nation. Key political figures led this process.

quiz.question: What does 'reunification' mean for Cameroon's history?
options: Joining the French and British Cameroons into one country
quiz.explication: Reunification joined the French and British administered Cameroons into one nation.

quiz.question: Who tells Ekwalla about Cameroon's independence story?
quiz.explication: Ekwalla's grandfather shares this important historical story with him.

quiz.question: Why is it valuable to communicate history across generations?
options: It preserves important knowledge and identity
quiz.explication: Communicating history across generations preserves knowledge and national identity.

lecons.contenu:
Independence and Reunification of Cameroon

What you will learn:

  • Trace the origin of Cameroon's independence
  • Explain the reunification of Cameroon
  • Appreciate the importance of key political figures

Learning family history in Douala (Level III syllabus, History: Political Evolution of Cameroon), Ekwalla hears about independence and reunification.

lecons.titre: Bilingualism and the Political Figures of Cameroon
savoirs_faire: Explain the bilingual nature of Cameroon
Identify some key political figures in Cameroon's history
Accept differences and opinions of other people

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog's class discusses how Cameroon communicates in both French and English as an officially bilingual nation, and learns about the political figures who shaped this unique national identity.
exercices.astuce: Cameroon is officially bilingual, using both French and English. Political figures throughout history have shaped the country's laws, unity and identity.

quiz.question: What does it mean that Cameroon is 'bilingual'?
options: It officially uses both French and English
quiz.explication: Cameroon is officially bilingual, using French and English.

quiz.question: What role did political figures play in Cameroon's history?
options: They shaped the country's laws, unity and identity
quiz.explication: Political figures shaped Cameroon's laws, unity and national identity.

quiz.question: Why is it important to accept different opinions of others?
quiz.explication: Accepting different opinions builds mutual understanding and respect.

lecons.contenu:
Bilingualism and the Political Figures of Cameroon

What you will learn:

  • Explain the bilingual nature of Cameroon
  • Identify some key political figures in Cameroon's history
  • Accept differences and opinions of other people

Discussing national identity in Douala (Level III syllabus, History: Political Evolution of Cameroon), Ngo Mbog learns about bilingualism and political figures.

lecons.titre: The Second World War and the United Nations
savoirs_faire: Explain the causes and consequences of the Second World War
Describe the role of the United Nations
Show willingness to settle disputes peacefully

exercices.enonce: Bikoy's teacher explains how the Second World War affected the world, including Cameroon under Trusteeship, and how the United Nations was formed afterwards to help countries communicate and settle disputes peacefully.
exercices.astuce: The Second World War had major global causes and consequences. Afterwards, the United Nations was created so countries could communicate and resolve disputes without war.

quiz.question: What international organisation was created after the Second World War?
quiz.explication: The United Nations was created after the Second World War.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of the United Nations?
options: To help countries communicate and settle disputes peacefully
quiz.explication: The United Nations helps countries communicate and resolve disputes peacefully.

quiz.question: What status did Cameroon have related to World War II's aftermath?
quiz.explication: After WWII, Cameroon had Trusteeship status under international administration.

lecons.contenu:
The Second World War and the United Nations

What you will learn:

  • Explain the causes and consequences of the Second World War
  • Describe the role of the United Nations
  • Show willingness to settle disputes peacefully

Studying 20th century history in Douala (Level III syllabus, History: The Second World War), Bikoy learns about the UN's role in global communication and peace.

lecons.titre: Class 5 Social Studies Year-End Review
savoirs_faire: Review key Social Studies concepts learned across the year
Communicate historical and civic knowledge confidently
Show pride in Cameroon's history and identity

exercices.enonce: As the school year ends, Ndombe's class reviews everything learned: early civilizations, explorers, German occupation, Renaissance, national emblems, and the political evolution of Cameroon — proud communicators of their nation's story.
exercices.astuce: Reviewing the year's Social Studies topics helps connect history, geography and citizenship into a fuller understanding of Cameroon and the world.

quiz.question: Which topic was NOT studied in Class 5 Social Studies this year?
quiz.explication: Detailed ocean marine biology was not a Social Studies topic; emblems and civilizations were studied.

quiz.question: Why is reviewing the year's Social Studies topics useful?
options: It connects history, geography and citizenship together
It is a waste of time
It only repeats old information uselessly
quiz.explication: Reviewing connects different topics into a fuller understanding.

quiz.question: What can pupils be proud of after a year studying Cameroon's history?
options: Their nation's rich story and identity
quiz.explication: Pupils can take pride in understanding their nation's rich history and identity.

lecons.contenu:
Class 5 Social Studies Year-End Review

What you will learn:

  • Review key Social Studies concepts learned across the year
  • Communicate historical and civic knowledge confidently
  • Show pride in Cameroon's history and identity

Wrapping up the school year in Douala (Level III syllabus, Social Studies year-end review), Ndombe's class reflects proudly on all they have learned.

lecons.titre: Conditional Actions and Broadcasting in Coding
savoirs_faire: Create conditional actions in a coding program
Recognize that conditional actions constitute the base for computer programs
Use broadcast blocks to make sprites communicate

exercices.enonce: Bikoy programs his sprite in Douala: 'if the sprite touches the wall, then it bounces back.' He also uses a broadcast block so one sprite can signal another sprite to start moving.
exercices.astuce: A conditional action follows an 'if...then' rule: if something happens, then do something else. Broadcasting sends a signal from one part of a program to another, helping sprites communicate.

quiz.question: What is a conditional action in coding?
quiz.explication: A conditional action follows an 'if...then' rule: if something happens, then do something.

quiz.question: What does 'broadcasting' do in a coding program?
options: Sends a signal so sprites can communicate
quiz.explication: Broadcasting sends a signal that other parts of the program (or other sprites) can respond to.

quiz.question: Why are conditional actions important in computer programs?
options: They are the base for how programs make decisions
quiz.explication: Conditional ('if...then') actions form the basic decision-making structure of computer programs.

lecons.contenu:
Conditional Actions and Broadcasting in Coding

What you will learn:

  • Create conditional actions in a coding program
  • Recognize that conditional actions constitute the base for computer programs
  • Use broadcast blocks to make sprites communicate

Making two sprites communicate in Douala (Level III syllabus, Basic Notion of Computational Thinking), Bikoy uses conditions and broadcasting to bring his program to life.

lecons.titre: Debugging: Finding and Fixing Program Errors
savoirs_faire: Recognize that computer programs can have errors that can be fixed
Practice basic debugging of a simple program
Show patience and problem-solving when programs don't work

exercices.enonce: Ndombe's sprite doesn't move as expected — with her teacher's help, she checks each block step by step in Douala and finds the mistake: two blocks were connected in the wrong order. She fixes it and the program works.
exercices.astuce: Debugging means finding and fixing errors ('bugs') in a program. Checking each step carefully helps find where something went wrong.

quiz.question: What does 'debugging' mean?
options: Finding and fixing errors in a program
quiz.explication: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing errors ('bugs') in a program.

quiz.question: What helped Ndombe find her program's mistake?
options: Checking each block step by step
quiz.explication: Checking each step carefully is a key debugging strategy.

quiz.question: Why is it useful to know that programs can have fixable errors?
quiz.explication: Knowing errors can be found and fixed encourages patience and persistence.

lecons.contenu:
Debugging: Finding and Fixing Program Errors

What you will learn:

  • Recognize that computer programs can have errors that can be fixed
  • Practice basic debugging of a simple program
  • Show patience and problem-solving when programs don't work

Fixing a broken program in Douala (Level III syllabus, Basic Notion of Computational Thinking), Ndombe learns the value of careful debugging.

lecons.titre: Sources of Information & Tools for Communication
savoirs_faire: Identify sources of information (books, newspapers, radio, TV, internet)
Identify tools for sending and receiving information
Compare different ways information can be communicated

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla lists the sources of information his family uses in Douala: books, newspapers, the radio, television, and the internet, then compares tools for sending messages: phone calls, texts, and email.
exercices.astuce: Information can come from many sources: books, newspapers, radio, TV, and the internet. Tools for sending and receiving information include phones, texts, and email.

quiz.question: Which of these is a traditional (non-digital) source of information?
quiz.explication: A newspaper is a traditional, printed source of information.

quiz.question: Which of these is a tool for sending and receiving information quickly online?
quiz.explication: Email is a digital tool for sending and receiving information.

quiz.question: Why is it useful to know different sources of information?
options: To choose the best source for what you need
Newspapers are the only real source
quiz.explication: Knowing different sources helps you pick the most reliable or convenient one for your needs.

lecons.contenu:
Sources of Information & Tools for Communication

What you will learn:

  • Identify sources of information (books, newspapers, radio, TV, internet)
  • Identify tools for sending and receiving information
  • Compare different ways information can be communicated

Comparing information sources at home in Douala (Level III syllabus, Internet and Communication), Ekwalla explores where information comes from and how it travels.

lecons.titre: Basic Concepts of Algorithm & Class 5 ICT Year-End Review
savoirs_faire: Explain the basic concept of an algorithm (step-by-step problem solving)
Review key ICT skills learned across the year
Show confidence using ICT tools responsibly

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog writes an algorithm for making tea, step by step: boil water, add tea leaves, wait, pour, add sugar. Her class then reviews everything learned this year: computers, storage, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, internet safety, and coding.
exercices.astuce: An algorithm is a set of step-by-step instructions to solve a problem or complete a task, just like a recipe. Reviewing regularly helps connect everything learned across the year.

quiz.question: What is an algorithm?
options: A set of step-by-step instructions to solve a problem
quiz.explication: An algorithm is a step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem or complete a task.

quiz.question: What everyday example is similar to an algorithm?
quiz.explication: A recipe, with its ordered steps, is a simple real-life example of an algorithm.

quiz.question: Which of these was NOT studied in Class 5 ICT this year?
quiz.explication: Cooking a full meal is not an ICT topic; Word, PowerPoint, internet safety and coding were all studied.

lecons.contenu:
Basic Concepts of Algorithm & Class 5 ICT Year-End Review

What you will learn:

  • Explain the basic concept of an algorithm (step-by-step problem solving)
  • Review key ICT skills learned across the year
  • Show confidence using ICT tools responsibly

Wrapping up the school year in Douala (Level III syllabus, Basic Notion of Computational Thinking + year-end review), Ngo Mbog connects algorithms to everyday life and reviews her ICT year.
